business_model.claim: BioCryst's primary commercial product is ORLADEYO (berotralstat), an oral, once-daily plasma kallikrein inhibitor approved for preventing hereditary angioedema (HAE) attacks in capsule and oral pellet formulations.
quotes: We have built a robust commercial infrastructure to support the successful commercialization of ORLADEYO, an oral, once-daily therapy discovered and developed internally for the prevention of HAE attacks.

In December 2025, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (“FDA”) approved an oral pellet formulation of once-daily ORLADEYO for prophylactic therapy in pediatric patients with HAE aged 2 to <12 years, and in October 2026, the FDA approved the 150 mg oral pellet formulation of once-daily ORLADEYO for prophylactic therapy in adults and adolescents aged 12 years and older.
This approval enables prescribers to offer their patients a more personalized treatment choice with ORLADEYO in either capsule or pellet form.

quotes: RAPIVAB (peramivir injection) is approved in the United States for the treatment of acute uncomplicated influenza for patients six months and older.
Peramivir injection is also approved in Canada (RAPIVAB), Australia (RAPIVAB), Japan (RAPIACTA), Taiwan (RAPIACTA), and Korea (PERAMIFLU).

business_model.claim: In the United States, BioCryst distributes ORLADEYO to patients through a sole-source specialty pharmacy partner, transitioning in Q3 2026 to CareMed, which takes title and maintains 7-21 days of inventory prior to dispensing.

competitive_position.basis: stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K, Q3 2026 Form 10-Q, and Q3 2026 earnings release
competitive_position.claim: ORLADEYO is the first oral, once-daily plasma kallikrein inhibitor commercialized for hereditary angioedema and the first and only targeted oral prophylactic therapy for children aged 2 to <12 years.
quotes: BioCryst has commercialized ORLADEYO® (berotralstat), the first oral, once-daily plasma kallikrein inhibitor, and is advancing a pipeline of potential first-in-class or best-in-class therapeutics for rare diseases.
ORLADEYO is the first and only targeted oral prophylactic therapy for children with HAE aged 2 to <12 years.

competitive_position.basis: stated directly in the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q and Q3 2026 earnings release
competitive_position.claim: BioCryst expanded ORLADEYO's regulatory footprint with FDA approval of an oral pellet formulation for pediatric patients aged 2 to <12 years in December 2025, marketing approval in Japan for that pediatric group in August 2026, and FDA approval of 150 mg oral pellets for patients aged 12 years and older in October 2026.
quotes: In December 2025, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (“FDA”) approved an oral pellet formulation of once-daily ORLADEYO for prophylactic therapy in pediatric patients with HAE aged 2 to <12 years, and in October 2026, the FDA approved the 150 mg oral pellet formulation of once-daily ORLADEYO for prophylactic therapy in adults and adolescents aged 12 years and older.
Additionally, in August 2026, Japan’s Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare granted marketing approval for ORLADEYO for prophylactic therapy in pediatric patients with HAE aged 2 to <12 years.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the 2025 Form 10-K summarizing 2025 company announcements
competitive_position.claim: Company surveys and real-world data support ORLADEYO adoption, showing 97 percent of 60 surveyed HAE treaters considering prescribing it, 70 percent of surveyed U.S. HAE patients strongly preferring oral prophylaxis (up from 50 percent in 2023), and substantial attack-rate reductions across over 350 patients in an underserved HAE segment.
quotes: On February 24, 2025, we announced that a new market tracking survey of 60 HAE treaters showed that 97 percent are considering prescribing ORLADEYO and 59 percent (up from 26 percent 18 months prior) of current prescribers indicate they are extremely likely to prescribe for more of their patients.

On May 5, 2025, we announced that the percentage of U.S. HAE patients who describe a strong preference for an oral prophylaxis therapy increased to 70 percent, up from 50 percent in 2023, in our latest market survey of HAE patients.

On August 4, 2025, we announced that new real-world data from over 350 patients with HAE with normal C1 inhibitor showed substantial reductions in attack rates with ORLADEYO, which we believe reinforces its value for a historically underserved patient segment and provides strong evidence to close gaps in both treatment and reimbursement.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the 2025 Form 10-K, Q3 2026 Form 10-Q, and Q3 2026 earnings release
competitive_position.claim: ORLADEYO revenue grew from 437,660 (table in thousands) in 2024 to 601,839 (table in thousands) in 2025 and reached $481,382 (table in thousands) in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, with full-year 2026 guidance maintained at $625 million to $645 million and management projecting global peak annual net revenue potential of $1 billion.
quotes: Based on proprietary analyses of HAE prevalence and market research studies with HAE patients, physicians, and payors in the United States and Europe, and five full years of commercialization experience with ORLADEYO, we anticipate that the global commercial market for ORLADEYO has the potential to reach a global peak of $1 billion in annual net ORLADEYO revenues.

The company maintained its outlook for full year 2026 global net ORLADEYO revenue of $625 million to $645 million and increased its full year 2026 total revenue outlook, including revenue from RAPIVAB® (peramivir injection) and the licensing of navenibart European rights, to $715 million to $730 million.
